transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Cascade Head of Cloud Security), Rajesh Singh (Platform Engineer), Olivia Park (Legal), Ben Torres (Product)

---
Summary (auto): weekly security check-in for POC - focus on SSO, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts, encryption, and next steps.
---

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick agenda, we'll cover SSO status, audit logging and retention, SOC2 artifacts, KMS/encryption, and then confirm actions.
00:22 - Speaker 2 (Laura): Sounds good. We're about to go into our pen test window next week, so any dependencies change?
00:28 - Speaker 1 (Maya): good note, we'll sync on that. Ethan will go over SAML playback and logs.
00:34 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): cool, hi all. quick status: we sent the metadata last friday, the IdP handshake succeeded in our staging for two users, there was one attribute mapping mismatch - email vs userprincipalname - which we adjusted.
00:52 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): we saw the metadata but our IdP team flagged the audience URI was using the internal hostname, is that expected?
00:58 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): ah, yes, there was a placeholder in staging that kept the internal FQDN, that's been fixed; prod will use the canonical route redwood-inference dot com slash sso.
01:12 - Speaker 2 (Laura): ok good. second question on SSO: can we enforce SCIM or just SAML for provisioning? we want to avoid manual account sprawl.
01:22 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): currently our POC supports SAML-only for auth; we can enable SCIM in a dedicated deployment — it's an add-on. For the pilot we can script provisioning via API, I'll share the script.
01:38 - Speaker 1 (Maya): to clarify, for cascade's pilot we offered a SAML flow plus a short-lived API key for seeding accounts; SCIM would be part of dedicated contract.
01:48 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): that's ok for now, as long as provisioning is repeatable.
01:54 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): legal quick interjection — for SSO we need to confirm session timeout defaults and ability to change them, and whether SAML assertions can include role claims for RBAC.
02:04 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): session timeout is configurable per-tenant on Dedicated and in our private deployments; in hosted we have defaults but can adjust for enterprise customers. SAML role claims are supported; mapping table is in the SSO guide. i'll drop links.
02:20 - Speaker 2 (Laura): great. moving on to audit logs — we need full request/response logs for inference calls, but redacted PII. what's your model?
02:30 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we capture structured audit logs: request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token counts, caller id), and optionally request/response bodies — those are off by default. we can enable body logging to a customer-controlled S3 or push to your SIEM over syslog/Kinesis.
02:48 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): push to our S3 bucket is preferred. retention? we need 12 months by default, with WORM for compliance.
02:58 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we support configurable retention windows; hosted default is 90 days but we can export and store to your bucket for 7+ years if needed. WORM is possible on the storage side; Redwood can sign and timestamp exports.
03:16 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): and about PII redaction — can the logs be redacted server-side before export? we can't have raw transcripts of customer messages leave the environment.
03:28 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, we offer field-level redaction rules; there's an option to omit request/response bodies entirely. additionally, we can apply regex-based scrubbing and replace detected PII with tokens. for pilot we'll provide a sample scrubbed log.
03:46 - Speaker 2 (Laura): what's the latency/cost impact of enabling body logging and scrubbing? our product team is sensitive to per-token costs.
03:56 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): overhead is small for metadata-only logs; body logging increases storage and a little CPU for scrubbing, so cost is storage + small processing fee. we'll include estimates in the log sample spreadsheet.
04:14 - Speaker 1 (Maya): i'll attach the spreadsheet and sample logs after the call.
04:20 - Speaker 6 (Ben): curious — do you ingest logs into Splunk or Datadog out-of-the-box?
04:26 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we have native exporters for both; also support S3/Syslog/BigQuery.
04:34 - Speaker 2 (Laura): SOC 2 — can you walk through what artifacts we'll get and timelines? we need Type II report and certain evidence for our auditors.
04:44 - Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for our hosted platform, report is recent (Q3 2025). we'll send the cert and the full report under NDA.
04:54 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): will you provide bridge letters or subservice auditor letters for specific controls?
04:59 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we can provide our SOC 2 report and cover letter; for more granular evidence (e.g., configuration snapshots) we'll coordinate with compliance — sometimes redacted screenshots are possible. i'll note this as an action.
05:14 - Speaker 6 (Ben): are there any outstanding remediation items from the SOC review?
05:20 - Speaker 1 (Maya): nothing material for customers; there were internal remediation items in our infra backlog but not blocking.
05:26 - Speaker 2 (Laura): KMS/integration — we need assurance that keys can be customer-managed for private deployments; for hosted, we prefer CMEK if possible.
05:36 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): for Private deployments you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM/KMS. For hosted we support CMEK for dedicated customers; for pilot, we can demonstrate envelope encryption and key rotation policies.
05:52 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): can we rotate keys without downtime?
05:56 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, key rotation is seamless with envelope encryption; we'll share documentation.
06:04 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): data residency question — can logs and model artifacts be kept in-region? we have customers in EMEA with residency requirements.
06:12 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, we can route storage to region-specific buckets and offer private deployments in your VPC region. for the pilot, we can keep everything in us-east unless you request otherwise.
06:24 - Speaker 2 (Laura): for Cascade we need EU-only storage for certain lines of business; we'll flag which data must stay in region.
06:30 - Speaker 1 (Maya): noted. please send a list of services/data types.
06:36 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): one technical deep-dive — how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching for multi-tenant logs? want to ensure no cross-tenant leakage.
06:46 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): isolation is per-tenant; KV cache is namespace-isolated, and the runtime enforces strict keys. we've got tests for cross-tenant isolation; i'll share the test summary.
07:00 - Speaker 2 (Laura): great. next — retention and deletion: if we need to purge customer data mid-contract, what's the process and timeline?
07:10 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we support on-demand purge; hosted takes up to 48 hours to scrub indexes and storage; for dedicated/private it's faster since you control storage. we'll provide a purge playbook.
07:22 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): legal will want attestations that purge is complete and logs of purge actions.
07:30 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we can provide audit entries for purge operations and signed statements.
07:36 - Speaker 6 (Ben): any SLA implications for forensic access during the pilot?
07:40 - Speaker 1 (Maya): pilot won't change our support SLAs for critical incidents; we'll agree on a runbook for the POC.
07:46 - Speaker 2 (Laura): good. two more quick things: vulnerability scanning and pen tests — do you have public results or do we need to rely on third-party scans?
07:58 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): we run regular internal scans and annual third-party pen tests; we can provide summary reports and remediation timelines under NDA.
08:10 - Speaker 2 (Laura): please share the last two test summaries.
08:14 - Speaker 1 (Maya): action item captured.
08:18 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): onboarding question — when we run a small benchmark of latency for our flows, will you share a per-route latency breakdown and tokens cost?
08:28 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, Redwood Console provides per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown, and traces. for the pilot we'll enable trace sampling and share the dashboard.
08:40 - Speaker 6 (Ben): what's the plan for canarying model updates during the POC? we don't want unexpected quality regressions.
08:48 - Speaker 1 (Maya): we recommended pinning to a model version for the pilot and allowing controlled rollouts; Redwood supports A/B and canary with automatic fallback.
08:58 - Speaker 2 (Laura): ok thanks.
09:02 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): quick legal item — DPA redlines. we've sent some comments; any updates?
09:08 - Speaker 1 (Maya): we received them, legal is reviewing. Olivia, do you want to sync with our counsel next week?
09:14 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): yes please, let's put that on the calendar.
09:18 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): back to logs, we'll prepare a sample of scrubbed logs and a mapping doc for fields and retention buckets.
09:26 - Speaker 2 (Laura): sample logs should include redaction examples and show how PII gets tokenized.
09:32 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): will do.
09:34 - Speaker 1 (Maya): any blockers from your side for the pilot to continue?
09:38 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): only the SAML attribute mapping confirmation and a small network egress config for our test bucket.
09:44 - Speaker 6 (Ben): from product side, we want to test the quality monitoring alerts tied to our evaluation suite. can you hook to our prompt sets?
09:54 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): yes, Redwood Optimize supports tie-in to evals; share the prompt set and we'll run a baseline and set alert thresholds.
10:04 - Speaker 1 (Maya): recap of actions: send SOC2 report, provision SAML test env, sample scrubbed logs and retention options, KMS docs, schedule pen test summary review, legal sync on DPA.
10:18 - Speaker 2 (Laura): timeline for SOC2 delivery?
10:22 - Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll send it today under NDA, expect to have docs in your portal by EOD tomorrow.
10:28 - Speaker 5 (Olivia): we'll review and send redlines for DPA by next monday.
10:34 - Speaker 4 (Rajesh): i'll confirm bucket config and share IAM role for S3 ingestion.
10:40 - Speaker 3 (Ethan): i'll ship the SAML metadata and provisioning script by tomorrow, plus the sample logs.
10:46 - Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and update the POC tracker in the portal.
10:52 - Speaker 2 (Laura): thanks.
10:55 - Speaker 1 (Maya): bye all.

---
